summary.title: Astro
summary.one_liner: Astro is a JavaScript web framework for fast, content-driven sites that renders components on the server and ships little or no client JavaScript, started with npm create astro@latest.
keywords: how to build a fast website with javascript
takeaways: Astro renders components on the server and sends lightweight HTML, aiming for minimal JavaScript on the client.
Islands architecture lets interactive UI components load independently while the rest of the page stays static HTML.
Content Collections give Markdown and MDX built-in TypeScript type-safety and frontmatter validation.
Astro supports multiple UI frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Preact, Solid, Qwik) and one-line deployment config for major hosts.

The page cites HTTP Archive and Chrome UX Report data showing Astro sites with the highest share of good Core Web Vitals among compared frameworks (71% vs. 48% WordPress, 45% Gatsby, 35% Next.js, 28% Nuxt).
summary.summary: This is the marketing homepage for Astro, a JavaScript web framework aimed at content-driven sites. It describes the main features: server-rendered components, islands architecture, content collections, framework-agnostic UI support, view transitions, image optimization, routing, middleware, type-safe server functions, and hosting adapters. It also lists a Core Web Vitals comparison against WordPress, Gatsby, Next.js and Nuxt, citing HTTP Archive and Chrome UX Report data. The page is mostly promotional and includes few technical details, so it works best as a quick overview rather than a tutorial.
